en: Evaporation of seawater in Manila Bay leaves solid salt crystals behind when the liquid water turns into gas.
Galvanized iron roofs in rural Philippines undergo a chemical change called rusting when exposed to heavy rain and oxygen.
Floodwaters in the Pasig River form a heterogeneous mixture where solid soil particles are temporarily suspended in liquid water.
Solid virgin coconut oil undergoes a physical change to become a clear liquid when left under the hot Philippine sun.
Granulated sugar completely dissolves in calamansi juice to form a homogeneous liquid mixture called a solution.
Decomposing carabao manure in rural biogas digesters produces methane gas, which is used as a flammable fuel for cooking.
Microorganisms cause a chemical change that ferments sweet sugarcane juice into sour Ilocos vinegar over several weeks.
Cold halo-halo drinks cause water vapor in the warm air to undergo condensation into liquid droplets on the glass.
Highly porous pumice stones ejected from Taal Volcano float on the lake because their overall density is lower than water.
Construction workers use a metal sieve to physically separate larger river pebbles from finer sand particles in the Cagayan River.
Burning dried rice husks in a farm produces ash and smoke, demonstrating an irreversible chemical change called combustion.
Bamboo handles on traditional cooking utensils remain cool because bamboo is a poor conductor of thermal heat compared to metal.
